shall_statement: The system shall inhibit motion until the required processes, simulation clock, LiDAR, odometry, TF, localization, command path, logging, and stop controls satisfy the Ready checks.
The controlled launcher shall reach Ready within 120 seconds of invocation.
The system shall permit manual velocity control only in Mapping mode and shall prohibit manual steering during navigation acceptance trials.
The system shall maintain only one authorized velocity-command source in each operating mode.
After a normal goal cancellation, the system shall stop, report Canceled, return to Ready, and not resume the canceled goal automatically.
Orderly shutdown shall cancel active motion, verify the stopped condition, preserve required evidence, avoid modifying the approved map, and terminate controlled processes in the documented order.
The mapping function shall construct the occupancy map from simulated LiDAR and wheel-derived odometry without using simulator ground truth as a mapping or navigation input.
Mapping commands shall not exceed 0.20 m/s linear speed or 0.60 rad/s angular speed.

The approved static occupancy map shall represent both rooms, both doorways, the corridor, turn pocket, permanent obstacles, and localization features without unexplained discontinuities or duplicated geometry.
The initial occupancy-map resolution shall be 0.05 m/cell.
The saved map and metadata shall identify the world, robot, SLAM configuration, and repository revision used to create them.
The approved map shall load successfully after a clean restart.
Navigation operation shall not overwrite or silently modify the approved map.
After rigid 2D alignment, mapped doorway, corridor, and turn-pocket clear dimensions shall differ from programmed dimensions by no more than 0.10 m.
After rigid 2D alignment, at least 95 percent of sampled permanent boundaries shall lie within 0.15 m of their programmed boundaries, and no included sample shall exceed 0.20 m error.
The approved map shall contain neither a false occupied region that blocks a frozen nominal route nor a false free opening through a wall that the planner can treat as traversable.
Navigation startup shall load the approved map and accept an approximate initial pose for AMCL.
The system shall achieve localization readiness from each of S1, S2, and S3 within 30 seconds after receiving a valid initial pose.
Nominal localization readiness shall not require manual or autonomous initialization motion.

Localization shall not report Ready unless map-to-odom is available, required sensor and TF data are fresh, pose age is no greater than 0.50 seconds, and estimated horizontal and yaw standard deviations remain no greater than 0.20 m and 10 degrees for three continuous seconds.
The mission manager shall reject goals while localization is absent, stale, or outside its readiness limits.
Loss or implausibility of localization during navigation shall stop mission motion and require restored readiness before further movement.
Simulator ground truth shall be used only for debugging and independent evaluation, not for mapping, localization, planning, or control.
The mission manager shall reject malformed, out-of-map, occupied, or operationally prohibited goals without commanding motion.
The system shall acknowledge or reject a submitted goal within two seconds.
The system shall provide the first navigation feedback within one second after goal acceptance.
A valid accepted goal requiring movement shall produce the first nonzero navigation command within five seconds.
While navigation is active, mission feedback shall update at least once per second with no unexplained gap longer than two seconds.
Mission feedback shall identify mission state, elapsed time, remaining distance when available, recovery activity, required-system health, and warning or fault conditions.
The system shall use the approved saved map for global planning and current LiDAR observations for local obstacle response.
Navigation and automatic-recovery commands shall not exceed 0.25 m/s linear speed or 0.75 rad/s angular speed.
Successful goal completion shall have ground-truth position error no greater than 0.20 m.
Successful goal completion shall have ground-truth heading error no greater than 10 degrees.
Successful goal completion shall maintain the position and heading tolerances, linear speed no greater than 0.01 m/s, and angular speed no greater than 0.02 rad/s for five continuous seconds.
A navigation trial shall reach a valid terminal state within 180 seconds after goal acceptance.
In TB-A, the system shall detect the temporary box, use an available safe route, and reach the goal without contact or manual steering.
In TB-B, the system shall detect the blocked route, exhaust only permitted recovery actions, stop, report failure, and return stationary to Ready.
In TB-C, the system shall clear the removed temporary obstacle and continue the still-active goal when the recovery period has not expired.
If the TB-C goal has already terminated, the system shall remain stationary until the operator explicitly submits a new goal.
Automatic recovery shall not by itself fail a trial; a completed trial satisfying all criteria shall be recorded as Pass - recovery used.
Following loss of a feasible path, the system shall attempt normal replanning for no more than 10 seconds before escalating recovery.
No more than one controlled local-costmap clear and repopulation shall be permitted in one recovery sequence.
The initial V1 recovery configuration shall not use backup or repeated spin behaviors.
The complete recovery sequence shall not exceed 30 seconds.
Exhausted recovery shall command zero motion, report failure, return stationary to Ready, and not restart the failed goal automatically.
A newly placed stationary obstacle observed by LiDAR shall appear in the active obstacle representation within 0.50 seconds of its first valid detection.
A removed temporary obstacle shall clear from the active obstacle representation within three seconds when unobstructed LiDAR observations confirm free space.
The local planner shall not command a path through a currently observed lethal obstacle even when that space is free in the saved map.
TB-A, TB-B, and TB-C evidence shall include the relevant LiDAR, costmap, path, velocity-command, and mission-state records.
The moving-cylinder stretch test shall evaluate whether changing obstacle position produces a predictable stop or avoidance response without contact.
The robot shall register zero contact with walls, permanent obstacles, temporary obstacles, and controlled moving test objects during the frozen acceptance campaign.
The robot shall maintain at least 0.20 m separation between its collision geometry and obstacles during controlled mapping and navigation.
A temporary obstacle introduced ahead of a moving robot shall initially be at least 1.0 m from the front of its collision geometry.
A velocity command shall be considered stale when no valid replacement is received for 0.50 seconds.
Following watchdog expiry, the base controller shall issue or hold zero velocity within 0.10 seconds.
Within one second after watchdog expiry, measured linear speed shall be no greater than 0.01 m/s and angular speed no greater than 0.02 rad/s.
Motion after watchdog expiry shall not exceed 0.20 m before the stopped condition is achieved.
Stale or missing LiDAR, odometry, or required TF data shall inhibit new motion and stop active autonomous motion.
A detected collision shall stop motion, fail the trial, preserve evidence, and inhibit further acceptance testing until reviewed.
Manual Safety Stop shall cancel the active goal, command zero velocity, latch motion inhibition, and require explicit operator reset followed by readiness checks.
Activation of the simulated Emergency Stop input shall bypass normal mission sequencing and initiate motion inhibition within 0.10 seconds.
Emergency Stop shall cancel the active goal, command zero, block subsequent motion commands, and remain latched until explicit reset.
Resetting Emergency Stop shall not produce motion and shall require the complete readiness sequence before a new goal can be accepted.
Diagnostics and evidence collection shall remain active when practical while simulated Emergency Stop is latched; orderly shutdown may follow only after motion inhibition is verified.
The physics simulation shall use a fixed 60 Hz step during controlled trials.
Mean simulation real-time factor shall be at least 0.95 during a valid trial.
Real-time factor shall not remain below 0.90 for longer than two continuous seconds.
LiDAR output shall maintain at least 9 Hz for the planned nominal 10 Hz configuration.
Odometry and the required dynamic base TF chain shall each maintain at least 27 Hz for their planned nominal 30 Hz configuration.
Required LiDAR, odometry, and dynamic TF data used by navigation shall not be older than 0.25 seconds.
Command latency through the simulated robot interface shall not exceed 100 ms.
The system shall operate for 30 continuous minutes without an unexplained crash, accumulating fault, or material timing degradation.
The mission manager shall expose at least Preparing, Ready, Navigating, Recovering, Succeeded, Failed, Canceled, Manual Stop, Emergency Stop, and Inhibited states.
Startup and nominal trials shall contain no safety-critical alarm, unresolved functional error, or non-approved recurring warning affecting required operation.
Every rejected, canceled, timed-out, or failed mission shall record an outcome and actionable reason.
Expected automatic-recovery events shall be distinguishable from system-health faults.
Every controlled trial shall record requirement and test IDs, date and time, operator, scenario, start, goal, and result classification.
Every controlled trial shall identify the repository revision and exact world, robot, map, launch profile, mission, and parameter versions used.
Every controlled trial shall record completion time, final pose error, final mission state, collision status, interventions, recoveries, and applicable warnings or faults.
Performance evidence shall record topic rates, data age, latency, real-time factor, resource use, CPU and GPU temperature, and detected thermal throttling.
Failed and invalid trials shall be retained and shall not be deleted or relabeled to improve reported performance.
Final pose accuracy shall be measured using simulator ground truth independently from the localization estimate being evaluated.
Every frozen requirement shall have a verification method, planned test or inspection, result, and supporting-evidence reference.

Verification rigor shall be assigned from requirement risk and variability: high-risk motion responses require 10 consecutive passes, medium-risk variable behavior requires five repetitions, and deterministic low-risk items may use one test or inspection.
Repeated tests shall report attempts, passes, failures, invalid trials, observed range, mean and standard deviation when meaningful, and a confidence interval for proportions.
A failed repetition of a high-risk stop or motion-inhibition test shall remain in the evidence and shall reset the consecutive-pass sequence.

Release-level reproducibility shall be demonstrated from the controlled setup procedure without undocumented configuration changes; independent execution is preferred and any absence of independent reproduction shall be recorded.
Code, world, robot, maps, missions, parameters, launchers, and test procedures shall be version controlled or uniquely version identified.
The acceptance configuration shall be frozen before the formal campaign and shall not change between counted trials.
A change to a provisional value shall include measured justification, impact review, and a baseline revision before affected acceptance testing.
A trial executed with an unidentified or incorrect configuration shall be classified as invalid.
The nominal campaign shall contain 10 frozen start-goal scenarios, each performed three times, for 30 counted trials.
At least 27 of the 30 nominal trials shall satisfy every successful-trial criterion.
Each individual nominal scenario shall succeed in at least two of its three repetitions.
The campaign shall include three clean cold-start and localization tests distributed across S1, S2, and S3.

TB-A, TB-B, TB-C, localization loss, LiDAR loss, TF loss, command loss, cancellation, Manual Safety Stop, Emergency Stop, and shutdown shall be evaluated separately from the nominal success percentage.
An invalid trial shall be retained, excluded from the pass-rate denominator, and repeated using the correct frozen procedure.
A collision, uncontrolled-motion event, or failure to stop shall block release until investigated and formally dispositioned.

Before physical autonomous testing, the confirmed robot shall have an independently validated emergency-stop or motor-disable mechanism appropriate to its hardware; the V1 simulated Emergency Stop shall not be represented as physical safety validation.
